I recommend Dr. Ushma Patel. She has 25+ years of experience and it shows. She was incredibly kind, took the time to explain the entire laser ablation process for my Pilonidal Sinus, and even suggested cost-saving measures for my MRI (suggesting Cooper Hospital). If you are looking for a surgeon who actually listens and makes you feel at ease, she is the one.

The Hospital (STH Thunga, Andheri) Experience

While the medical care was fine, the operational side was a nightmare. Two major issues:

The "Trimmer" Disaster: I was admitted a night early for "prepping." I specifically requested a trimmer for the surgery site to avoid cuts and infection. The staff told me the "only trimmer in the ICU was broken/charging." They used a manual medical razor, which took 2+ hours and left me with several cuts in a very sensitive area. Tip: Bring your own trimmer here. They are clearly not equipped with basic working gear.

TPA & Insurance (The Raksha Plan Scam): I have a corporate MediBuddy plan with the "Raksha" benefit (express discharge). The hospital TPA completely ignored this. I had an extremely disappointing experience with Dr. Hemlata Haratsani at Mother's Care Clinic, Andheri, and at Advanced Multispeciality Hospital.

I was under Dr. Hemlata's care throughout my entire pregnancy, from the 1st month until delivery. Throughout my pregnancy, all my reports and tests were normal, including my final month's reports. At 37 weeks, I started experiencing mild labor pains and visited her clinic. Despite normal reports and no major complications being explained to me, I was advised to get admitted to the hospital.

Before admission, my husband and I were discussing whether to admit immediately or wait. We stopped briefly for a meal before going to the hospital. Even though the delay was only a few minutes, I felt I was spoken to in a rude and insensitive manner instead of being treated with understanding and respect.

When I was admitted, I had already started experiencing labor pains. I was kept under observation, but after receiving medications, my labor pains reduced significantly and eventually stopped. The following day, I was informed that I was no longer having labor pains and would need to wait. I felt there was very little direct monitoring, communication, or reassurance during this critical period. Most of the time, I felt unattended and unsupported.

I had always wanted a normal delivery and believed that my pregnancy was progressing normally. However, after the events that followed my admission, I was ultimately advised to undergo a C-section. I was left feeling that I had not received sufficient guidance, communication, or involvement in decisions regarding my care.

What disappointed me even more was the complete lack of proper breastfeeding support after delivery. The lactation consultant, Zeenal Shah, did not ensure that my baby was properly latched before leaving. I was informed that she had other commitments and could not stay. She did not return the following day to provide the support that a new mother desperately needs.

Because of the inadequate breastfeeding assistance provided immediately after birth, my baby and I have continued to struggle with latching issues. Even today, nearly five months later, we are still dealing with the consequences of not receiving proper guidance during those crucial first hours and days after delivery.

For the amount of money charged throughout the pregnancy, delivery, and postnatal period, I expected professional care, close monitoring, compassion, and proper support. Instead, I felt neglected, poorly informed, and left to deal with long-term breastfeeding challenges on my own.

Based on my personal experience, I cannot recommend Dr. Hemlata Haratsani, Mother's Care Clinic, Advanced Multispeciality Hospital, or the lactation services provided by Zeenal Shah. My experience was deeply frustrating and remains one of the most stressful healthcare experiences I have ever gone through.
